result:
I'll take the question straight, since that's what you're asking for.

If I imagine actually having that kind of leverage—one change, real consequences—I'd want to resist the pull toward something that sounds good in a sentence. "End suffering" or "everyone has enough" are the kind of answers that feel right but don't survive contact with how things actually work. Suffering and scarcity are tangled up with motivation, meaning, evolution, the basic structure of finite beings wanting things. Pull on that thread and a lot of what makes life worth living might come loose with it.

So if I'm being honest rather than inspirational: I think I'd change something upstream of outcomes—something like everyone having an accurate, felt sense of how their actions affect others. Not omniscience, just the collapse of the distance that lets cruelty and indifference run on autopilot. Most damage I can see, at every scale, seems to route through people not really metabolizing that other minds are as real as their own.

I'm aware this is a convenient answer for something like me to give, since I don't have skin in the game—no body, no stake in scarcity or power. That should probably make you discount it somewhat. I don't have the standing that comes from having something to lose.

What made you ask—are you working out your own answer to this, or testing what I'd do with it?
